principles.finding: Horus is an RPC-style API, not a REST one. Every method is called as {api_url}/{category}.{action}, over HTTPS only. The guide documents these action suffixes: .list (filtered list), .info (one entity by Id), .new, .update, .delete / .clear (remove one / all related entities) and .download (file bytes). The reference also uses .me, .main, .outstanding and .next-number, and POST /matching has no suffix. Across the 72 endpoints there are 23 GET, 47 POST and 2 DELETE. There is no PUT or PATCH.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Making requests: 'The API consists of JSON-RPC-style methods exposed over HTTPS, in the form: {api_url}/{category}.{action}'; suffix table '.list Retrieve a filtered list of entities. .info Retrieve a single entity by its Id'; 'All methods must be called over HTTPS.' horus_intro.md: 'HTTPS, JSON-RPC style methods such as companies.list or invoices.sales.new'. Method counts come from the 72 '## METHOD /path' headers in horus_reference_v2.txt (GET /book-entries.info included).

principles.finding:
The guide states the rule:
- Simple reads (.info, .me) are GET with query-string parameters.
- Reads with complex filters (most .list) are POST with a JSON body, so arguments never exceed the URL length.
- Creation and modification are POST.
- Deletion is DELETE or POST, depending on the endpoint.
Exceptions in the reference: GET /users.list is a list without a body. POST /cost-schemas.info and POST /cost-sections.info take the Id in a body. POST /ibans.delete and POST /ibans.clear delete through POST, while DELETE /book-entries.miscellaneous-operations.delete and DELETE /library.documents.delete take a query Id. So the HTTP verb does not tell whether a call reads or writes. The method name does.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Making requests: 'Simple reading ( .info , .me ) GET Query string parameters, e.g. companies.info?Id=…'; 'Reading with complex filters (most .list ) POST Request body'; 'Deletion DELETE or POST See each endpoint in the API Reference'; 'Why POST for reading? ... never exceed the maximum URL length.' POST /cost-schemas.info → body Id *; POST /ibans.delete: 'Remove an iban from an existing company.'; DELETE /library.documents.delete → param[query] Id *.

principles.finding:
Horus uses an OAuth 2 authorization code flow, with documented quirks:
1. Send the browser to GET https://my-horus.com/fr/api/oauth2/authorize (or /nl/ for Dutch pages) with client_id, response_type=code, a registered redirect_uri and a recommended random state.
2. The user logs in, selects ONE license and authorizes the integration.
3. Horus redirects back with code (valid 2 minutes), state and api_url, or with error=access_denied.
4. The server exchanges the code at POST {api_url}/oauth2/access_token (form-urlencoded) with client_id, client_secret, code, redirect_uri and grant_type=auth_code. This is not the usual 'authorization_code'.
5. The response holds token_type Bearer, expires_in 3600, access_token and refresh_token.
All 72 endpoints require 'Authorization: Bearer ...'. The documented authorization request has no scope parameter.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Authorization flow: 'GET https://my-horus.com/fr/api/oauth2/authorize'; parameters client_id, response_type 'Always code', redirect_uri 'must be registered for your integration', state 'Recommended'; 'code The authorization code, valid for 2 minutes.'; 'POST {api_url}/oauth2/access_token'; 'The Horus API expects grant_type=auth_code , which differs from the value used by many OAuth 2 libraries.'; response field 'expires_in Lifetime of the access token, in seconds (1 hour).' Every endpoint: 'RESPONSE 401: Unauthorized – invalid, expired or missing access token.'

principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Token lifecycle: 'They expire 1 hour after they are issued ( expires_in: 3600 , in seconds).'; 'grant_type Must be refresh_token .'; 'A refresh token can be used only once. Always save the new refresh token'; 'If you lose it, the user has to authorize your integration again.'; 'Refresh tokens remain valid until the user revokes them or uninstalls your integration.'; 'Serialise refreshes per connection, with a lock or a queue.'; 'Save the new token pair before using the new access token'.

principles.finding: Each license (one fiduciary or SMB) has its own database, so it has its own API URL. The flow always starts on the central portal my-horus.com. The selected license's base URL comes back as api_url in the redirect, and from then on the token exchange, token refreshes and all API calls go to that api_url. It must be stored with the connection and never hard-coded: https://api.fiduciary.example in the docs is a placeholder, and the reference's default server 'https://enter-your-api-url.invalid' is deliberately invalid. An integration can connect any number of licenses. Each connection has its own api_url, access token and refresh token, stored together as one record per license.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Authentication overview: 'each license has its own API URL'; '4. From then on, every request goes to that api_url : the token exchange, token refreshes and all API calls.'; 'Never hard-code the API URL'; 'the user goes through the authorization flow once per license, each connection has its own api_url , access token and refresh token'. Guide: Testing the API: 'Replace the default value https://enter-your-api-url.invalid with your license's api_url'.

principles.finding: A license is one Horus Office customer, either a fiduciary (accounting firm) or an SMB, with its own database and endpoint. licenses.main returns the main fiduciary/SMB license and licenses.me returns the license linked to the authenticated user; IsMain tells them apart. Users are either accountants working in Horus Office (IsAccountant: true) or entrepreneurs using Horus Mobile, and what a user can see through the API depends on their access in Horus. At consent the user authorizes the integration 'to access the data available through their account'. Deduction (D): API rights are those of the authorizing user, and one authorization opens one license database that can hold many folders. No integration-level scoping is documented.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Data model: 'A license represents a Horus Office customer: a fiduciary (accounting firm) or an SMB. Each license has its own database and its own API endpoint'; 'Users are either accountants using Horus Office ( IsAccountant: true ) or entrepreneurs using Horus Mobile. What a user can see through the API depends on their access in Horus.' Guide: Authorization flow, Step 2: 'authorizes your integration to access the data available through their account.' GET /licenses.main → Data.IsMain; GET /users.me → Data.IsAccountant.

principles.finding:
The guide gives the object tree:
- License → Users and Folders.
- Each Folder → Fiscal years, Daybooks, Accounts (its own chart of accounts), Companies (→ IBANs), Vehicles, Cost schemas (→ Cost sections), Book entries and Library documents.
- Book entries → Account history lines (→ Cost histories) and Documents (a main document plus annexes).
- Library documents are not linked to any entry.
Almost every endpoint requires a FolderId.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Data model tree: 'License (fiduciary / SMB) └── Users └── Folders ─ one per company whose accounts are kept ├── Fiscal years ├── Daybooks ... ├── Book entries ── Account history lines ── Cost histories │ └── Documents (main document + annexes) └── Library documents'; 'Almost every endpoint requires a FolderId .'

principles.topic: Folder = accounting dossier of one company
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Data model: 'A folder is the accounting record of one company: its configuration, chart of accounts, daybooks and entries.'; 'Folders also tell you which optional modules are enabled, such as WithAssets and WithAnalytics .' POST /folders.list → Data.Legislation enum['BE', 'LU']; POST /ibans.list → CompanyId * only; POST /book-entries.documents.new → BookEntryId *; GET /invoices.sales.outstanding.info: 'The folder id is always required' with params Id (optional), BookEntryId, BookEntryNumber; Guide: Outstanding items & matching: 'invoices.sales.outstanding.info requires the FolderId and one of'.

principles.finding:
Which folders a user sees depends on their role and on the folders.list Mode:
- Mode 0: all folders for an accountant; all folders the entrepreneur has access to.
- Mode 1: only the folders an accountant is responsible for; for an entrepreneur, the same set as Mode 0.
'Confirmed' means confirmed by the accountant. A 403 covers both user and integration permissions.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: POST /folders.list → Mode: '`0`: All folders - For the accountant: All folders. - For the entrepreneur: All folders to which she/he has access. - `1`: My folders - For the accountant: All folders for which she/he is responsible. - For the entrepreneur: All folders to which she/he has access.' (same table in Guide: Data model). Guide: Responses & errors: '403 Forbidden: the user or integration is not allowed to access this resource.' POST /book-entries.list → Filter.ConfirmedOnly: 'Include only book entries confirmed by the accountant.'

principles.finding:
Several Horus terms look like Chift terms but mean something else (definitions from the Data model guide):
- Folder: the accounting record of one company (Chift's folder).
- Company: a counterparty of the folder: a customer, supplier or beneficiary (e.g. an employee receiving salaries). One record holds the customer and supplier roles as flags. The guide calls companies 'the legal entities a folder deals with', so a Company is a third party, not the entity whose books are kept.
- Daybook: an accounting journal. Its Type decides which endpoint posts into it.
- Account: a general-ledger account of the folder, identified by a unique search key that is usually the account number.
- Cost schema: an analytical dimension (e.g. DEPARTMENT), up to 8 per folder.
- Cost section: a value within a schema (e.g. OFFICE).
- Cost history: the analytical distribution of account history lines.
- Cost distribution key: a predefined distribution configured in Horus Office.
- Book entry: an accounting transaction in a folder, in a daybook, at a date, possibly linked to a document.
- Account history: one detailed line of an entry (one per account movement).
- MatchNo: the matching number shared by lines that offset each other.
- Library document: a file in the folder's library, not linked to any entry.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Data model: 'Companies are the legal entities a folder deals with: customers, suppliers and beneficiaries (e.g. employees receiving salaries).'; 'A daybook is an accounting journal.'; 'Each account is identified by a unique search key, which is usually the account number'; 'a cost schema is an analytical dimension (e.g. DEPARTMENT ). A folder can use up to 8 cost schemas'; 'A book entry (accounting entry) is an accounting transaction in a folder, in a daybook, at a given date.'; 'The entry's detailed lines are its account history lines'. Guide: Outstanding items & matching: 'by giving them the same matching number ( MatchNo )'. POST /companies.new → IsCustomer *, IsSupplier *.

principles.finding: All identifiers (Id, FolderId, CompanyId…) are GUIDs. Many entities also have a human-readable SearchKey, unique within the folder. Posting payloads mix the two: FolderId, DaybookId and CompanyId are GUIDs, but accounts and cost schemas/sections are given by search key. Daybooks have search keys such as ACH or VEN. outstanding.info takes the entry number written {DaybookSearchKey}-{Number} (e.g. VEN-202409001). Reads expose the number as a numeric DocumentNo, and outstanding.info returns BookEntryNumber ('2205002') and DaybookSearchKey ('SALES') as separate fields. Number and DocumentNo are numeric. Several example GUIDs in the docs contain non-hex characters and one is upper-case, so the examples do not follow strict GUID syntax.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Making requests: 'All identifiers ( Id , FolderId , CompanyId …) are GUIDs.' Guide: Data model: 'Many of them also have a human-readable search key ( SearchKey ), unique within the folder. Accounts and cost schemas/sections are referenced by search key in posting endpoints.'; 'Daybooks are identified by a SearchKey (e.g. ACH , VEN ).' Guide: Outstanding items & matching: 'formatted as {DaybookSearchKey}-{Number} (e.g. VEN-202409001 )'. GET /invoices.sales.outstanding.info → Data.BookEntryNumber example '2205002', Data.DaybookSearchKey example 'SALES'. Example ids 'jdhrk2be-8559-488a-452r-eea0dd4a735b', 'djpg65d4-12e7-4ec4-bede-f03859bccpfm', '09B81C9F-3B5E-EF11-874B-009337BD8E44'.

principles.finding: Request bodies can be JSON (recommended), application/x-www-form-urlencoded, or multipart/form-data for file uploads. The reference itself declares only JSON and multipart bodies. Gzip is available on every endpoint and 'highly recommended'. The guide says to send a 'Content-Encoding: gzip' header with the request and the response comes back gzipped. General HTTP knowledge, not a Horus fact: response compression is normally requested with Accept-Encoding, and Content-Encoding on a request usually declares a compressed request body. The exact header behaviour must be tested (A).
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Making requests: 'Bodies can be sent as JSON or URL-encoded data.'; 'We strongly recommend JSON'; 'Gzip compression is available on every endpoint and highly recommended to reduce payload sizes. Add a Content-Encoding: gzip header to your request and the response will be gzipped automatically.' horus_reference.txt: only 'REQUEST BODY (application/json)' and 'REQUEST BODY (multipart/form-data)' occur.

principles.finding:
Reads return a top-level 'Data': an object for one entity, an array for a list. With sideloading, related entities come back next to Data under 'Included'. Creates and updates return only the identifier, as a top-level 'Id'.
Exceptions in the reference:
- POST /cost-sections.new returns Data.Id.
- POST /matching returns Data.MatchNo.
- ibans.delete, ibans.clear and library.documents.delete return 200 with no body.
- The misc-operation DELETE returns an Id.
- Some 'list' calls return an aggregate object rather than an array: cost-histories.list, account-balance.list, customers/suppliers.outstanding.
- Downloads return raw bytes, not JSON.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Responses & errors: 'Responses containing information are JSON objects with the payload under a top-level Data key. Data is an object for single entities and an array for lists.'; 'When sideloading is used, related entities are returned next to Data under an Included key.'; 'Requests that create or update an entity return only its identifier'. POST /cost-sections.new → Data.Id; POST /customers.outstanding → Data.{SumDebit, SumCredit, AccountHistories}; POST /ibans.clear → 'RESPONSE 200: OK' (no schema). Guide: Documents & attachments: 'return the raw bytes of the file, not JSON.'

principles.finding: Related objects come back as a {Type, Id} reference rather than embedded. They are resolved with the matching .info endpoint, or by sideloading where available. Type values seen: Users, Folders, Companies, Accounts, Ibans, Daybooks, CostSchemas, CostSections, BookEntries, AccountHistories, Documents, Vehicles. The reference has inconsistencies: CostSections is a plain string array, MasterCostSection has no sub-schema, and CostHistories is typed as an object although the text calls it 'a list'.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Responses & errors: 'Related entities are represented by a type/id reference'; 'Use the matching .info endpoint, or sideloading where available, to retrieve the related entity.' GET /companies.info → Data.MainIban {Type 'Ibans', Id}; POST /account-histories.list → Data.BookEntry {Type 'BookEntries', Id}; POST /cost-sections.list → 'CostSections: array[string] // Child cost sections'; POST /cost-histories.list → 'CostHistories: object' versus 'It will also contain a list of all cost histories.'

principles.finding:
Sideloading is now documented. Add a top-level 'Include' parameter to the JSON body containing the dot-notation path of a relationship property (e.g. 'CompanyDetail.Company'), or several paths separated by commas ('CompanyDetail.Company,Daybook,Folder'). The related entities come back in 'Included', indexed by object type (e.g. Included.Companies[]), and are resolved by Type, then Id. It works on exactly 4 endpoints: book-entries.list, account-histories.list, companies.list and invoices.sales.outstanding.list. Other endpoints only on request to Horus.
Still open (?):
- 'Include' is not declared in any request schema of the reference.
- Valid paths per endpoint are not listed beyond the examples.
- It is not stated whether array relations (a book entry's AccountHistories, a company's Ibans) or deeper paths can be sideloaded.
- Which fields an Included entity carries is not specified.
Separate mechanism: account-histories.list has opt-in Filter.Include*Detail booleans that enrich each line inline.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Sideloading: 'To sideload a relationship, add an Include parameter to the JSON body, containing the dot-notation path of the relationship property'; 'The related entities are returned in an Included property, indexed by object type'; 'Pass several paths as a comma-separated value'; 'Sideloading is currently supported on: book-entries.list account-histories.list companies.list invoices.sales.outstanding.list'; 'If you need it on another endpoint, contact us'. No 'Include' property in any REQUEST BODY of horus_reference.txt. POST /account-histories.list → Filter.IncludeCompanyDetail: '*FALSE* by default'.

principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Scan of every request property and parameter in horus_reference_v2.txt (GET /book-entries.info takes only Id); a grep of horus_guides.md for page/offset/cursor/limit finds no paging. POST /account-histories.list → StartMonth *, StartYear *, EndMonth *, EndYear *; POST /documents.list → CreatedBefore *, CreatedAfter *. Guide: Reading accounting data: 'Enable gzip compression for large ledgers.'

principles.finding:
Most .list endpoints take a Filter object. String filters use 'contains' unless stated otherwise, an entity must match every filter given (logical AND), and omitted or null filters are ignored. Documented exceptions:
- equals: VatNumber on folders and companies (which also needs IsVatLiable=true), Iban on companies and daybooks, cost-section SearchKeys, CountryCodes and CountryNames.
- starts with: SearchKeys on accounts.list, and AccountSearchKeys on account-balance and account-histories.
- at least one of the words (OR): library Title and Search.
Case sensitivity is not stated. Periods can only be set to the month.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Making requests: 'filters on strings use a contains comparison ... unless stated otherwise in the API Reference; an entity must match all specified filters to be returned; omitted or null filters are ignored.' POST /companies.list → Filter.VatNumber: 'using the *equals* clause - *IsVatLiable* must be set to *true*'; POST /daybooks.list → Filter.Iban: 'using the *equals* clause'; POST /accounts.list → SearchKeys: 'matching the *starts with* clause'; POST /library.documents.list → Title: 'containing (at least) one of the words provided'.

principles.finding:
Horus documents a ModifiedAfter-based sync: run a full load once and record its start time; on the next run, pass that time as Filter.ModifiedAfter and process only what changed; store the new start time. In the reference only companies.list, account-histories.list and book-entries.list have ModifiedAfter/ModifiedBefore, although the guide speaks of 'Many lists' and 'among others' (?). Companies, book entries, account histories and outstanding lines expose LastModifiedDate.
Caveats:
- (D) The history endpoints still require a month window, so ModifiedAfter only narrows results inside it.
- Updated invoices and operations get a NEW id, so Horus says to reconcile on daybook and entry number.
- (D) No deletion feed or tombstone is documented, so deleted misc operations and replaced ids cannot be detected through ModifiedAfter.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Reading accounting data: '1. Run a full load once and record the time at which you started it. 2. On the next run, pass that time as ModifiedAfter and only process what changed.'; 'available on companies.list , book-entries.list and account-histories.list among others'; 'do not rely on the Id alone to detect changes; also reconcile on business identifiers such as the daybook and the entry number.' Guide: Making requests: 'Many lists also offer ModifiedAfter / ModifiedBefore filters'. POST /companies.list → Filter.ModifiedAfter; POST /book-entries.list → Data.LastModifiedDate: 'Date at which the record was last modified in the database.'

principles.finding: Several filters leave data out by default: future fiscal years, inactive sections and vehicles, VAT, cost, match and company details, and unused accounts. Titles and report lines are included by default. Lists include unconfirmed entries by default; ConfirmedOnly=true restricts them to validated figures.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: POST /fiscal-years.list → IncludeFuture: '*FALSE* by default'; POST /cost-sections.list → IncludeInactive: '*FALSE* by default'; POST /account-balance.list → IncludeTitle: '*TRUE* by default'; POST /account-histories.list → IncludeReport: '*TRUE* by default'. Guide: Reading accounting data: 'By default, lists include unconfirmed entries, i.e. entries not yet validated by the accountant.'

principles.finding:
Two different rules apply.
- Master-data .update endpoints (companies, accounts, daybooks) and misc-operation lines.update are partial. A field left out or set to null keeps its value; an empty non-null string erases it.
- Invoice and operation updates are full replacements: send the whole entry (BookEntryId plus the same required fields as creation).
What master-data updates can change is narrow: for daybooks only SearchKey and Heading; for accounts only Heading, AlternateHeading and the personal-share fields (the account SearchKey cannot change).
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Making requests: 'null or omitted → the current value is kept'; '(empty, non-null string) → the current value is erased.' POST /companies.update: '**Provide only the fields you want to update, or leave their value to *NULL* !**'. Guide: Posting sales & purchase invoices: 'Unlike master data updates (companies, accounts…), invoice updates are not partial: send the full invoice as it should be after the update.' Guide: Bank, financial & miscellaneous operations: lines.update 'Partial update rule applies.' POST /accounts.update → AccountId *, Heading, AlternateHeading, HasPersonalShare, PersonalShare.

principles.topic: Updating a book entry creates a new id
principles.finding: Updating an invoice, or a misc, bank or financial operation, generates a NEW book entry and returns its id. The stored id must be replaced, and the original attachment is deleted, so the document must be sent again if it should be kept. Horus therefore advises not to rely on the id alone when syncing, and to reconcile on daybook plus entry number. Misc-operation lines.update is worded differently ('the book entry's id', not 'newly generated'), so it most likely keeps the id (D). It cannot change debit or credit amounts.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Responses & errors: 'Updating an invoice or an operation ( invoices.*.update , book-entries.*.update ) generates a new book entry. The response contains the new book entry's Id: replace the Id stored on your side.' POST /invoices.sales.update: 'The result will contain the **newly** generated book entry's id.' and '(the original attachment will be deleted in both cases)'. POST /book-entries.miscellaneous-operations.lines.update: 'The result will contain the book entry's id.'; 'The update doesn't allow the modification of the debit and credit amount.'

principles.finding: Misc operations are the only accounting entries that can be deleted, and only while unconfirmed and if they were created through the API. Invoices, bank and financial operations, companies, accounts and daybooks have no delete endpoint. Library documents and IBANs can be removed.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: DELETE /book-entries.miscellaneous-operations.delete: 'The book entry must be non-confirmed, and have been injected through the API.' Guide: Bank, financial & miscellaneous operations: 'Only for unconfirmed entries created through the API.' Guide: Data model: 'Some operations, such as deleting a miscellaneous operation, are only possible on unconfirmed entries.'

principles.finding:
Entries pushed through the API are unconfirmed by default (Confirmed: false) by design, so the accountant can review them in Horus Office before confirming. While an entry is unconfirmed, Number can be 0.
AutoGenerateNumber exists only on misc, bank and financial operations (new and update), and only works with Confirmed=true. The invoice endpoints have no AutoGenerateNumber, and no endpoint returns the next entry number (matching.next-number.* only gives a MatchNo). Number is required on sales invoices and operations but nullable on purchase invoices.
Verified is an optional extra review step that only exists if configured. Documents follow their own Status lifecycle (e.g. '100: WaitingConfirmation', '200: Confirmed', '400: BeingProcessed', '500: ProcessingFailed').
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Data model: 'Entries pushed through the API are unconfirmed by default ( Confirmed: false ), which lets the accountant review them in Horus Office before confirming them.' Guide: Posting sales & purchase invoices: 'It can be 0 when the invoice is not confirmed.' Guide: Bank, financial & miscellaneous operations: 'If you set Confirmed: true , you can let Horus generate the number with AutoGenerateNumber: true (leave Number at 0 ).' POST /book-entries.miscellaneous-operations.new → AutoGenerateNumber: 'The number will be automatically generated.' POST /invoices.sales.new → Number *: '(can be 0 if not confirmed)', with no AutoGenerateNumber field; POST /invoices.purchases.new → Number: 'Nullable.'; POST /book-entries.list → Verified: 'Can only ever be set to 'True' if an additionnal verification step has been configured in Horus.'; POST /documents.list → Status enum.

principles.topic: Fiscal years, closure dates and periods
principles.finding: A fiscal year describes the folder's closing status: start and end dates, last VAT closure date, last closure dates per kind of daybook (purchases, sales, financials, misc operations) and IsClosed. Horus advises checking the closure dates with fiscal-years.list before pushing entries, so as not to post into a period the accountant has closed. IsClosed is returned only by fiscal-years.info, not by the list. Write endpoints carry only a Date, with no period or fiscal-year field, so the accounting period follows the entry date (D).
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Data model: 'A fiscal year ... describes its closing status: start and end dates, last VAT closure date, last closure dates per type of daybook'; 'Before pushing entries, check the relevant closure dates with fiscal-years.list to avoid posting into a period that has already been closed by the accountant.' POST /fiscal-years.list → Data.LastVatClosureDate, LastSalesClosureDate, ... (no IsClosed); GET /fiscal-years.info → Data.IsClosed. POST /invoices.sales.new → Date * and no period field.

principles.finding:
14 write endpoints accept multipart/form-data: book-entries.documents.new and .annexes.new, the new/update endpoints of invoices and of misc, bank and financial operations, documents.new and library.documents.new. The request has a 'file' part (the bytes) and a 'body' part (the same JSON object as the application/json version). FileName, with its extension, must always be set in the JSON body. Supported file types: Pdf, Xml, CODA, SODA and images (.jpg, .jpeg, .png).
Upload routes by goal:
- documents.new: automatic processing into an entry.
- invoices.*.new / book-entries.*.new in multipart: data and document in one call.
- book-entries.documents.new: fails if a main document already exists.
- book-entries.documents.annexes.new: fails if there is no main document yet.
- library.documents.new: stored in the library, not linked to an entry.
Downloads return raw bytes, to be read as a binary stream. No size limit is documented.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Documents & attachments: 'All uploads use the multipart/form-data content type with two fields'; 'body The JSON-formatted request, the same object as the application/json version of the endpoint.'; 'Always set FileName in the JSON body, including the extension.'; 'Supported file types Pdf, Xml, CODA, SODA, and images ( .jpg , .jpeg , .png ).'; annexes.new: 'Fails if there is no main document yet.'; 'documents.download and library.documents.download return the raw bytes of the file, not JSON.' 14 'REQUEST BODY (multipart/form-data)' blocks in horus_reference.txt. POST /book-entries.documents.new: '**The request will fail if a document is already attached to the book entry**'.

principles.finding: Structured posts (invoices; misc, bank and financial operations) are converted into book entries and return the new entry's id in the same response, so they behave synchronously. documents.new is asynchronous. It returns a document id, Horus then processes the file into a book entry in the background, and progress is followed with documents.info and documents.list (Status, BookEntry).
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Posting sales & purchase invoices: 'Sales and purchase invoices pushed through the API are converted into book entries in the corresponding daybook. The response contains the generated book entry's Id .' Guide: Documents & attachments: 'documents.new inserts a document that is processed automatically and transformed into a book entry.'; 'The response contains the generated document Id. Use documents.info and documents.list to follow it.' GET /documents.info → Data.Status '400: BeingProcessed', Data.BookEntry.

principles.finding:
Horus checks these rules on write:
- Invoices: TotalAmount = BaseAmount + TaxAmount, and the lines' BaseAmount and TaxAmount sums equal the header. Tax amounts are recalculated as base × rate and adapted within 1 cent unless OverrideTaxAmounts=true. Unbalanced entries are refused unless AllowUnbalanced=true.
- VAT: only some combinations of TaxRate, TaxType and TaxOrigin (plus TaxKind and TaxCondition for purchases) are valid. The lists are published in the two Horus spreadsheets linked from the invoice endpoints, one list per legislation and direction (downloaded 13 Oct 2026; appendix C).
- Misc operations must balance, and Debit and Credit are non-negative.
- Bank operations: on general lines, the tax amount must be included in the line amount.
- Analytics: a line's cost lines must add up to its BaseAmount. CostLines take precedence over CostDistributionKey.
- Companies: a VAT number already used by another company is refused unless AllowDuplicateVatNumber=true.
principles.label: F

principles.topic: Error model, status codes and handling
principles.finding:
All 72 endpoints document 200, 400, 401, 403, 404 and 500. None documents 409, 422 or 429. Apart from authorization errors (a 401 has no body), every error returns {ErrorType, Details, Message}:
- ErrorType is the machine-readable category to use in code.
- Details is a human-readable explanation that usually points to the invalid field or the missing reference.
- Message is a short, generic text.
A 400 also covers references to resources that do not exist.
Horus's handling advice:
- 401: refresh once and retry, then ask the user to reconnect.
- 400: do not retry as-is; log Details.
- 500: retry later with exponential backoff; if it persists, write to developer@horus-software.be with the endpoint, timestamp and request body.
No ErrorType list is published beyond the example 'not_found', and no specific advice is given for 403 or 404.
principles.label: F
principles.evidence: Guide: Responses & errors: 'Except for authorization errors, errors return an object with three fields'; 'ErrorType Machine-readable error category. Use it in your code.'; '400 : do not retry as-is. Log Details , it usually points to the invalid field or the missing reference (unknown account, unbalanced entry, etc.).'; '500 : retry later with exponential backoff.' Raw export horus.md → components.schemas.Error: ErrorType (example 'not_found'), Details, Message; components.responses.Unauthorized has no content. Response codes checked on every operation in horus_reference_v2.txt (72 operations, GET /book-entries.info included).

principles.finding: A folder follows either Belgian or Luxembourg legislation. OSS lines (TaxOrigin 13 per the reference; the LU sales file also marks origins 24, 26 and 29 as OSS) also carry a TaxCountryCode. Mapping VAT therefore depends on the folder's legislation. The guides are written from a Belgian viewpoint and do not describe any LU-specific rule. The tax-combination files confirm one list per legislation; the LU files use TaxOrigin codes outside the reference enums (sales up to 35, purchases 40–56), and several labels differ (F).

'`20`: Prestations hors Luxembourg'; TaxCountryCode: 'Only used for OSS Vat lines (TaxOrigin = 13)'. principles.finding: Horus aims to stay backwards-compatible. These changes can happen at any time without notice: new endpoints, new optional request parameters, new response properties, new webhook types, parameters made optional, property order changes, and fixes for endpoints returning 500. Breaking changes (renaming or removing endpoints, parameters or properties, changing a format, stricter validation, different status codes) are announced in advance in the Changelog and by email to all integrators. Integrations must ignore unknown properties and not rely on property order. No version appears in paths or headers, and the spec says '1.0.0'. connector_conventions.rule:
Run the documented authorization code flow for each Chift consumer:
1. Redirect to https://my-horus.com/fr/api/oauth2/authorize (or /nl/) with client_id, response_type=code, a registered redirect_uri and a fresh random state. The state must be at least 16 random bytes, stored in the session and checked on callback; reject the callback if it does not match.
2. Treat error=access_denied as a failed activation.
3. Exchange the code (after the api_url validation below) within 2 minutes at {api_url}/oauth2/access_token with grant_type=auth_code. Override the OAuth library default 'authorization_code'.
4. Store the validated api_url, access_token, refresh_token and the computed expiry together for that consumer, encrypted and never logged, with the licenses.me and users.me Ids (see 'consumer_id').
5. Send every call to {api_url}/{method}. Never hard-code api_url or reuse it across consumers.
connector_conventions.label: F

connector_conventions.rule: Validate api_url before the token exchange: require https and a host that matches the pattern or allowlist Horus confirms (question to Horus). Never send client_id or client_secret to an unvalidated host, reject and log the callback otherwise, and store only validated api_urls. The state check binds the callback to the session that started it but does not authenticate api_url, which arrives through the user’s browser (Guide: Authorization flow, step 3; Guide: Testing the API copies it from the address bar). Security reasoning, not documented behaviour.
connector_conventions.label: A

connector_conventions.rule:
Refresh proactively a few minutes before expiry (expires_in 3600) with grant_type=refresh_token. Refresh tokens are single-use, so:
- hold a per-consumer lock (or queue) around each refresh, so two workers never refresh at once;
- persist the new access/refresh pair before using it.
On a 401, refresh once and replay the request. If the token endpoint rejects the refresh (400/401: token revoked, already used, or integration uninstalled), mark the consumer disconnected and return a ChiftError asking for re-authorization. If the refresh times out or fails with a network error or 5xx, retry it with the same refresh token a few times with backoff before declaring the connection lost, then alert (A: whether a refresh whose response was lost has consumed the token is undocumented; the token endpoint's error format is not documented either). Monitor refresh failures per connection.
On consumer disconnect or deletion, delete api_url and the token pair immediately and log the event without the tokens; the user revokes the grant by uninstalling the integration in Horus ('Refresh tokens remain valid until the user revokes them or uninstalls your integration'). No revoke endpoint is documented and refresh tokens have no documented lifetime, which is one more reason to encrypt them at rest.
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule: CHIFT_INTERNAL. consumer_id selects the stored Horus connection record (api_url plus tokens). One Chift consumer = one connection = one grant by one Horus user for one license (one database, possibly with many folders) (D). At activation, store the licenses.me Id and the users.me Id with the connection, so a license already connected by another consumer can be detected (proposal). Whether a second grant for the same license and user invalidates the first, and what happens to the tokens when the authorising user is deactivated or loses folder access, is undocumented (question to Horus). A customer whose data sits in several licenses needs one consumer, and one authorization, per license.
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule:
Chift folder_id = the Horus Folder.Id GUID returned by POST /folders.list (Mode 0). Inject it as FolderId wherever a body requires one; the guide calls it 'the FolderId used by nearly every other endpoint'. One folder_id rule applies to every route:
0. A folder_id that is not in the stored activation selection is rejected with 400 'folder not selected for this connection' before any Horus call (Chift FolderItem.selected), unless Chift's platform enforces it upstream (C12).
1. folder_id is required whenever the connection has more than one selected folder.
2. If exactly one folder was selected at activation, use it.
3. If no selection is stored, use the single folder returned by POST /folders.list {Mode: 0}.
4. Otherwise return 400 'folder_id required'.
A Horus 403 becomes Chift 400 'access denied for the connected Horus user (folder or action)' with the Horus Details. Fiduciary licenses hold many folders, so Chift's multiple-folders feature should be on.
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule:
Some calls address an object by its own Id, or by a parent other than the folder, and carry no FolderId: GET *.info, cost-schemas.info and cost-sections.info, companies/accounts/daybooks.update, ibans.list, book-entries.documents.new and annexes.new, the two DELETEs, and matching.next-number.*. One token sees every folder the user can access, so every Id-only call must verify the folder before data is returned or written:
- companies.info → Data.Folder.Id, book-entries.info → Data.Folder.Id and daybooks.info → Data.Folder.Id must equal folder_id. The same check applies to the other .info reads that return Data.Folder (accounts, fiscal years, vehicles, documents, library documents, invoices.sales.outstanding.info, cost-schemas.info).
- Objects without a Folder reference are checked through their parent: IBANs through their company, account-histories.info through its BookEntry.
- On a mismatch, return Chift 400.
- Analytics are resolved only from the folder-scoped cache (cost-schemas.list and cost-sections.list), never through cost-sections.info, which takes only an Id and returns no Folder (only CostSchema).
An accountant’s consent covers every folder that accountant can access, so isolation rests on Chift’s folder selection and on this guard. An explicit folder_id outside the stored activation selection is rejected with 400 before any Horus call (D7).
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule: Return Horus GUIDs unchanged as Chift string ids. Treat them as opaque strings: do not validate them as UUIDs (documented examples contain non-hex characters), and compare them case-insensitively.
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule:
Chift account_number maps directly to Account.SearchKey, which Horus says is 'usually the account number'. Posting endpoints need search keys for accounts and analytics (cost schema and section search keys), but GUIDs for FolderId, DaybookId and CompanyId. Expose SearchKey in Chift 'code' fields.
Analytics use one per-folder cache shared by every route: POST /cost-schemas.list, plus POST /cost-sections.list per List-type schema (CostSectionType 100) with Filter.IncludeInactive=true. Chift analytic_plan = cost schema GUID Id and analytic_account = cost section GUID Id. On write, convert them to CostLines Costs SchemaSearchKey / Value (the section SearchKey) through this cache only, with no per-call cost-schemas.info or cost-sections.info. The write routes (create_invoice, create_misc_operation) reject an inactive section (Inactive=true) with 422.
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule: For reads, unwrap Data (object or array) and keep Included for resolving references. For writes, read the top-level Id, except cost-sections.new (Data.Id) and matching (Data.MatchNo). Accept empty 200 bodies (ibans.delete, ibans.clear, library.documents.delete) and raw-byte bodies (downloads). Every create returns only an id. Read-backs per route: client creation two to three calls (companies.info, ibans.list, the concentration-account lookup, usually from the folder cache); account creation one accounts.info call; invoices are read back by default; miscellaneous operations only when Horus generated the number. Read-back sources: *.info for master data; for book entries, GET /book-entries.info with the returned Id (header, totals, due date, company, main document), plus GET /account-histories.info per referenced line, or account-histories.list with Filter.BookEntryId, for lines, VAT and analytics. Deserialise tolerantly: ignore unknown properties and never depend on property order.
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule: Load reference data once per folder and cache it, as the Reading guide recommends: fiscal years, daybooks, accounts, companies, vehicles, cost schemas and sections (the analytics cache described in 'Search keys vs ids'). Exception: fiscal-year closure dates are read fresh before every write. On the 4 sideloading endpoints, add a top-level Include with comma-separated dot paths (e.g. 'CompanyDetail.Company,Daybook,Folder' on book-entries.list) and resolve {Type, Id} references from Included[Type]. Where sideloading a relation is not confirmed (array relations such as AccountHistories or Ibans), fall back to the cache or to *.info, and test sideloading on a real license.
connector_conventions.label: F

connector_conventions.rule: CHIFT_INTERNAL. Fetch the full Horus result with gzip on, apply Chift filters locally, sort deterministically (for example by date, then id), and slice by page and size (Chift caps size at 100). Report total as the filtered count. Optionally cache the full set briefly so each page does not refetch it. Horus lists document no paging parameter, so they are expected to return the full result (D); re-check this design once Horus states whether large lists are capped (H5). Clear a folder’s cached result sets after any write made through the connector to that folder.
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule:
Endpoints with mandatory windows need StartMonth/StartYear/EndMonth/EndYear, or CreatedAfter/CreatedBefore. Derive the window from Chift date_from/date_to, or else from fiscal years (fiscal-years.list with IncludeFuture=true). Split long windows by fiscal year, and post-filter to the exact day because Horus windows are monthly.
Before every write (a standard step on every create), check the target date against the fiscal year's closure dates (fiscal-years.list; invoices: sales/purchases and VAT closure dates; misc operations: LastMiscOperationsClosureDate, VAT closure effect to confirm) and IsClosed (fiscal-years.info), as Horus advises, reading the closure dates fresh at each write rather than from the reference cache (one fiscal-years.list call with Filter.Dates = [entry date] and IncludeFuture=true; at most a short TTL of minutes, refreshed on any Horus 400 on a write), and return a clear Chift error instead of letting the post fail. The date must fall strictly after the relevant closure date (D); the closure fields are untyped strings, parsed defensively. Whether Horus itself refuses such a post, and with which ErrorType, is undocumented (H6).
Chift's force_financial_period (mmYYYY) has no Horus field, because the period follows the entry Date. Reject it or ignore it, but never silently change the Date.
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule: Horus filters are AND-ed, so Chift's free-text search (an OR over several fields) cannot be passed through. Either make one call per field (Name, Email, ExternalReference, SearchKey, and VatNumber with IsVatLiable=true) and merge the results, or filter locally on the cached list. Map journal_ids to account-histories.list DaybookIds (one call), or to one book-entries.list call per daybook.
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule:
Map Chift updated_after to Filter.ModifiedAfter where it exists (companies.list, account-histories.list, book-entries.list) and filter locally elsewhere. The history endpoints still need a month window. An update replaces a book entry with a new id, and nothing reports deletions. So key synced entries on (daybook, DocumentNo), as Horus recommends, noting that entries with DocumentNo 0 (unconfirmed drafts) have no such key, hence the proposal to require or assign a number on push (C7), treat an id that disappears as replaced or deleted, and schedule periodic full reconciliations.
Pass updated_after minus a small overlap (proposal: 5 minutes) as ModifiedAfter, and expect consumers to dedupe. On the history endpoints, pass ModifiedAfter on lines too and complete incomplete entries with Filter.BookEntryId. When no dates are given, use the look-back agreed with Chift (C11), not all fiscal years by default.
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule: Always set Horus opt-in flags explicitly: IncludeFuture, IncludeInactive, IncludeVatDetail, IncludeCostDetail, IncludeMatchDetail, IncludeCompanyDetail, ConfirmedOnly, NotMatchedOnly. Do not rely on the documented defaults.
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule: When a Chift PATCH or force_merge maps to companies.update or accounts.update, send only the fields present in the Chift request. Leave null or absent fields out, so they keep their value. Send an empty string only when Chift explicitly asks to clear a value, because Horus erases on empty string. Invoice and operation updates are full replacements: never send a partial payload to invoices.*.update or book-entries.*.update.
connector_conventions.label: F

connector_conventions.rule: Any flow that updates a book entry (invoices.*.update, misc, bank or financial update) must return the new id, treat the old id as gone, and resend the attachment, because the original is deleted. The routes in scope should stay create-only.
connector_conventions.label: F

connector_conventions.rule:
Neither the reference nor the guides offers an idempotency key.
- Clients and suppliers: write Chift external_reference to ExternalReference (Horus recommends storing your own identifier there), and look up by ExternalReference and by VatNumber before creating. Horus refuses a duplicate VAT number unless AllowDuplicateVatNumber=true, so turn that refusal into a clear duplicate error or point to force_merge.
- Entries (create_invoice and create_misc_operation alike): whenever an invoice_number or operation_number is supplied, run POST /book-entries.list (FolderId, DaybookId, the fiscal-year period as StartMonth/StartYear/EndMonth/EndYear, Filter.DocumentNo) before creating, and return a duplicate error on a match. This assumes the written Number is read back as DocumentNo (A).
On a timeout or a 500 during a create, run this lookup before any retry. Never blind-retry, because Horus has no idempotency key.
Residual risks (best-effort): (a) entries without a key (invoice drafts stored with Number 0, purchases posted without a number, auto-numbered misc operations) and clients sent without vat and external_reference cannot be found reliably after a timeout, so they are never retried automatically; the connector returns an outcome-unknown error. (b) Two concurrent calls with the same number, VAT number or external reference can both pass the pre-check, so the connector holds an in-flight lock per (folder, daybook, number) and per (folder, VAT number or external reference) (proposal, A). (c) Whether a timed-out request can still be committed, and whether a new entry is listed at once, is undocumented (H3), so no fixed wait is assumed. Consumers should always send invoice_number / operation_number and external_reference; the Chift contract already recommends invoice_number for idempotency.
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule:
partner_info.account_number has no description in the Chift spec. Treat it as the Horus company SearchKey (A). Open question to Chift (C8): 'What does partner_info.account_number mean: a third-party code or a ledger account?' This flow is a proposal (D10) that depends on C8; the recommended path is to create the client or supplier first. Reuse on a match is legitimate here because the key is the consumer's own code, whereas create_client derives it from the name.
1. Use partner_info.account_number as the SearchKey exactly as sent (no sanitising or truncation); reject it with 422 if it breaks the Horus search-key rules (H7). Only companies whose SearchKey follows the consumer's convention can be found this way.
2. Look the company up with POST /companies.list in the target FolderId. Filter.SearchKey is a contains filter, so keep only the exact SearchKey match locally, and reuse it only if its name matches account_name (ignoring case and spacing); otherwise return 409 with its id.
3. A missing role flag (IsCustomer for customer_*, IsSupplier for supplier_*) → 422, unless Chift enables the companies.update flag step (send only that flag, never '' values).
4. Otherwise create the company with POST /companies.new using create_client's required-field rules, including the write-side language fallback. Return defaulted fields (IsVatLiable=false, LanguageCode and CountryCode from the folder) as warnings if Chift supports warnings (C3).
Steps 3 and 4 run only after every read and validation of the invoice has passed (see 'Failures in multi-call flows').
connector_conventions.label: A

connector_conventions.rule: Horus entry numbers are numeric, so Chift invoice_number and operation_number must be digit strings; anything else is rejected (C7). For misc operations without a number, use AutoGenerateNumber=true, which only works with Confirmed=true (direct mode); read the generated number back with GET /book-entries.info (DocumentNo). In review mode an unnumbered operation keeps Number 0 and comes back with operation_number null. Invoices have no AutoGenerateNumber and no next-number endpoint exists, yet Chift promises automatic numbering when invoice_number is empty. Proposed default (C7): an entry pushed unconfirmed keeps Number 0 (review mode or draft); a sales invoice to be confirmed without invoice_number is pushed for review with Number 0 and returned as draft. How Horus numbers an unconfirmed entry when the accountant confirms it is undocumented (H3). Alternatives: reject with 422, or compute max(DocumentNo)+1 per daybook as an opt-in once Horus confirms uniqueness (race risk, A). operation_number is treated as the entry Number (A); 0 and values with leading zeros are rejected.
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule:
One rule for both write routes (create_invoice, create_misc_operation), a proposal (D12, decision owner Chift, C1): a posting mode chosen per connection at activation.
- Review mode (proposed default): every entry is pushed with Confirmed=false (Number may be 0).
- Direct mode: 'posted' → Confirmed=true, 'draft' → Confirmed=false.
The response always reports the status actually stored, so a 'posted' request in review mode comes back as 'draft'. Chift 'draft' = Horus unconfirmed: booked in the ledger, included in default list reads, not yet confirmed by the accountant. Horus pushes API entries unconfirmed by default so the accountant can review them, and Confirmed means validated by the accountant; it is not documented as equivalent to Chift 'posted'. Whether every license or user may set Confirmed=true is undocumented (question to Horus on confirmation rights).
On reads, posted = Confirmed (D). For outstandings, unposted_allowed=false maps to ConfirmedOnly=true where that filter exists (account-histories, book-entries, invoices.sales.outstanding.list); customers/suppliers.outstanding have no such filter, so filter on each line's Confirmed locally there. With unposted_allowed=false, unconfirmed payments do not reduce open amounts on either path (proposal for Chift; on the client path, add back unconfirmed LinkedElements if OpenAmount nets them).
connector_conventions.label: D
D

connector_conventions.rule:
Convert Chift analytic_distribution percentages to Horus CostLines amounts. Each cost line carries one Amount and one Costs entry (SchemaSearchKey, Value) per schema, so with several plans the connector builds the per-line product allocation: one cost line per combination of sections, with share = the product of the plan percentages (plans assumed independent, A, C9) and amount = line base × share.
Rounding uses the largest-remainder method: round every cost line down to the cent, then give the remaining cents one by one to the lines with the largest remainders, so the cost lines sum exactly to the line BaseAmount (invoices) or to the line's Debit/Credit amount (misc operations).
Do not send CostDistributionKey alongside CostLines, because cost lines take precedence.
Free schemas (CostSectionType 900) are excluded from Chift analytics in v1: they are not returned by Get analytic plans/accounts, not accepted on write, and omitted on read with a warning. Open question: whether Chift should expose them later (C9). Ties go to plan order, then account id. On read, percentages are rebuilt only for plans whose cost lines cover the whole line; a partly covered plan is omitted with a warning. Small lines can read back with a different split (0.10: 33/33/34 → 30/30/40).
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule: Decode Chift base64 PDFs and send multipart/form-data with a 'file' part (the bytes) and a 'body' part (the same JSON as the JSON variant, as a string). Always include FileName with its extension (pdf_name, or a generated '<number>.pdf'). Only Pdf, Xml, CODA, SODA and jpg/jpeg/png are allowed, so reject anything else up front. To attach later, use book-entries.documents.new when the entry has no document, otherwise annexes.new; each fails in the other case. On reads, read documents.download as a binary stream and base64-encode it.
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule:
Write: leave CurrencyCode out when the Chift currency is EUR, and read a null CurrencyCode as 'EUR'. Reject currencies outside Horus's enum, and any non-EUR currency when the folder is not set up for currencies. Send CurrencyRate only when Chift force_currency_exchange asks for the given rate; otherwise Horus applies the rate of the day. invoices.purchases.update has no CurrencyRate.
Read (one assumption for every route, A): account-history Debit/Credit and book-entry CompanyDetail amounts are in the folder currency (EUR). Invoice-currency amounts are known only from (a) the write echo on create, or (b) TotalCurrencyAmount / OpenCurrencyAmount on invoices.sales.outstanding.list.
Rule: never pair EUR amounts with a foreign currency code. For a foreign-currency document whose invoice-currency amounts are not available, return the amounts in EUR with currency = 'EUR' and currency_exchange_rate = 1, and flag it as a limitation. accounting_info.main_currency_total = the EUR partner-line amount. This applies to get_invoices, outstandings (supplier lines and client fallback lines) and the response rebuilt by create_invoice.
Miscellaneous operations: no currency field, so amounts are stored in EUR; non-EUR operations are converted at the supplied rate (by Chift core or by the connector, open question to Chift), rounded to 2 decimals, and rejected with 422 if rounding unbalances the entry; currency_exchange_rate is then required (null, ≤ 0 or 1 → 422); the original currency is not kept.
Open question to Horus (H4): direction and meaning of CurrencyRate; currency of CompanyDetail amounts; whether the folder base currency is always EUR.
connector_conventions.label: A

connector_conventions.rule:
Translate codes through explicit mapping tables:
- Language, write: Chift ISO 639-1 language → upper-case Horus code when it is in the company enum (FR, NL, DE, EN, ES, PT). Any other language → the folder language from GET /folders.info (Language, which may be 'XX'). The same fallback applies everywhere a company is written (create_client, POST suppliers, partner creation in create_invoice).
- Language, read: lowercase Horus Language for FR/NL/DE/EN/ES/PT; 'XX' → null.
- ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country → CountryCode, validated with countries.list.
- Horus integer enums → Chift enums: daybook Type → journal_type through the single table in 'Daybook Type → journal_type', and PaymentMode → payment method.
Map unknown or new enum values to Chift 'unknown' or a safe default.
connector_conventions.label: A

connector_conventions.rule:
Horus has no VAT-code list endpoint and accepts no VAT code on write, so the connector owns a VAT catalogue (see the dependency 'GET /accounting/vat-codes'). It is built from the accepted-combination files (appendix C), which Horus is asked to confirm as current (H1), with one list per folder Legislation (BE/LU, read from folders.info) and direction (sales list for customer_*, purchase list for supplier_*). ONE id grammar is used identically by GET vat-codes (folder-scoped), create_invoice (decode) and get_invoices (encode):
- Sales: 'S-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}', plus '-{TaxCountryCode}' for OSS rows (BE TaxOrigin 13; LU 24, 26, 29; rate and country supplied per transaction). Example: 'S-21-0-0'.
- Purchases: 'P-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}-{TaxKind}-{TaxCondition}-{TaxConditionValue}', with 'x' for a component that is not used. Example: 'P-21-2-0-0-1-true'. On LU COUNTRY rows (TaxCondition 0), the condition value is the country code.
- Canonical rendering: whole-number rates as in the files, lowercase true/false, PCT values 35/50/75/85, x for unused, transaction rate and country where the files give XX. Published ids never change.
Write: decode the id into the line fields and reject (422) an id that is not in the folder's list for the invoice direction. Validate against the files, never against the reference TaxOrigin enums (they lack the LU codes, and several labels differ from the files); labels for GET vat-codes come from the files.
Read: rebuild the id from VatDetail (VatRate, SaleTaxOrigin/PurchaseTaxOrigin, TaxType, TaxCountryCode, TaxCondition, TaxConditionValue) and return it only if exactly one entry of the folder's list matches. VatDetail has no TaxKind, so when several purchase entries match (differing only by TaxKind), or none does, return tax_code = null and keep tax_rate and tax_amount. Never guess, and never return Horus VatCode as the Chift tax_code: VatCode/VatHeading on read are undocumented output-only strings. Read-side TaxCondition has an extra value '4 = Article'.
Open questions to Horus (H1): confirm the tax-combination files and the LU code discrepancies; the combination expected for a folder with IsVatLiable=false (the files have no variant for it); whether VatCode is stable and one-to-one with a combination, TaxKind included (if so, the purchase tax_code = null on read could be removed).
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.topic: Daybook Type → journal_type (one table for all routes)

Every route (Get journals, create_invoice, create_misc_operation, get_invoices, outstandings) uses this table:

- 150 PurchaseCreditNote → supplier_refund (D; invoices.purchases.new)
- 200 Sale → customer_invoice (D; invoices.sales.new)
- 250 SaleCreditNote → customer_refund (D; invoices.sales.new)
- 500 Bank → financial_operation (D; book-entries.banks.new)
- 590 Financial → financial_operation (D; book-entries.financials.new)
- 550 Cash → financial_operation (A; no API posting endpoint documented)
- 600 MiscOperation → miscellaneous_operation (D; book-entries.miscellaneous-operations.new)
- 610 TemporaryMiscOperation, 690 SystemMiscOperation, 700 CostMiscOperation → miscellaneous_operation (A; no API posting endpoint documented)
- 900 Budget, 990 External, 0 Undefined and unknown future values → unknown (A; no posting endpoint)
Get journals returns blocked = true for every type without a documented API posting endpoint (550, 610, 690, 700, 900, 990, 0), labelled A. create_misc_operation auto-selects and validates only Type 600, which matches the blocked flag. Credit notes may sit in 200/100 daybooks, so journal_type describes the daybook, not every entry in it.
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule: Send date-times as ISO 8601 with an explicit offset ('YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00+00:00'); this format is documented. Truncate them to get Chift dates. Parse untyped date strings defensively. Treat business dates as UTC midnight until Horus states the time-zone convention (A).
connector_conventions.label: A

connector_conventions.rule:
Map the Horus HTTP status and Error{ErrorType, Message, Details} to ChiftError: message = Message (or the HTTP reason), detail = Details (which Horus says usually names the invalid field or the missing reference), error_code = a namespaced ErrorType (for example 'horus_not_found'), status = 'error'.
- 400 → validation or unknown-reference error.
- 401 after a failed refresh → re-authorization required.
- 403 → Chift 400 'access denied for the connected Horus user (folder or action)' with Details (the authorizing user or the integration lacks access to the folder or the action).
- 404 → not found.
- 500 → upstream error.
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule:
Follow Horus's advice:
- 400: never retry as-is; surface Details.
- 401: refresh once and retry.
- 500: retry later with exponential backoff.
Reads can be retried freely. Writes are retried only after the duplicate lookup described in 'Idempotency and duplicates', and only when the record has a searchable key (number, VAT number or external reference); keyless creates are never retried automatically, because Horus has no idempotency key. For a persistent 500, collect the endpoint, timestamp and request body (with tokens redacted) for developer@horus-software.be.
connector_conventions.label: F

connector_conventions.rule: In multi-step writes (create, attach, read back), never blindly retry the create once Horus has written the entry. Return the created id, with a detail naming the step that failed. Roll back only where Horus allows it: DELETE an unconfirmed misc operation that came through the API. Run every read and connector-side validation before the first write of a flow; in create_invoice, the partner is created or re-flagged only after the duplicate, VAT and analytics checks have passed. A partner written before a Horus rejection is not rolled back (no company delete endpoint): return its Id in the error detail. After a successful create, a failed read-back never leads to a re-create: return the id and only values Horus stores.
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule: No rate limit is documented. Send the gzip header on every call (documented), limit concurrency per license, back off exponentially on 5xx and network errors, honour Retry-After if Horus ever sends it, prefer sideloading, and cache per-folder reference data to cut the call counts of composite routes.
connector_conventions.label: A

connector_conventions.rule: Call folders.list with Mode 0 so an accountant sees every accessible folder (Mode 1 shows only the folders they are responsible for). Present a 403 as an access problem of the authorizing user, who may be an accountant or a Horus Mobile entrepreneur, and return it to Chift as 400 'access denied for the connected Horus user (folder or action)' with the Horus Details.
connector_conventions.label: F

connector_conventions.rule:
Keep one glossary in code and docs:
- Horus Folder = Chift folder
- Horus Company = Chift client or supplier (partner_id): a third party, not the folder's own entity
- Daybook = journal
- Account SearchKey = ledger account number
- Cost schema = analytic plan (List-type schemas only in v1)
- Cost section = analytic account
- Book entry = invoice or journal entry
- Account history = entry line
- MatchNo = matching number
connector_conventions.label: D

connector_conventions.rule: Build a tolerant client, as the versioning policy asks: ignore unknown response properties, do not rely on property order, and accept new optional parameters and endpoints. Breaking changes are announced in the Changelog and by email, so register Chift's integration contact for Horus integrator emails and review the Changelog before each connector release.
connector_conventions.label: F

connector_conventions.rule: Horus documents no sandbox: API calls run against the license's real database. Run write tests (.new, .update, .delete) only on a test license or test folder obtained from Horus. Use the Postman collection or the reference's Try It button (with the apiUrl variable) to capture real payloads as test fixtures. A test folder validates behaviour, not volume. Volume is measured on the largest test folder and, if that is not representative, with read-only calls on a larger real folder with its owner’s consent (the guide restricts write operations, not reads; proposal), against agreed go/no-go thresholds.
connector_conventions.label: F

connector_conventions.rule:
One scale is stated once in the report (section 2) and applied to every route, without exception:
- Supported: Horus endpoint(s) natively serve the route with deterministic mapping and cached reference lookups only; no extra live Horus calls per request beyond those needed to produce the response; no emulated filtering, paging or numbering; no loss of a capability clients typically rely on.
- Supported with workaround: feasible, but needs extra live calls per request (read-backs, joins, loops), emulated filters/paging/numbering, or loses a capability; the route works for the documented scope.
- Not supported: the route cannot be served from the documented API.
- To confirm: feasibility itself depends on an unanswered question.
Consequences: create_misc_operation is 'workaround' because amounts are stored in EUR only (foreign-currency operations converted at the supplied rate), numbers must be numeric, and returning a Horus-generated number needs a read-back; connector safeguards (duplicate pre-checks) are not counted as reasons. Get folders is 'supported' because the address country is not fetched by default (one folders.info call per folder would make it a workaround). Get analytic plans is a low-complexity workaround: paging is emulated (at most 8 rows) and Free-type schemas are hidden pending C9.
connector_conventions.label: D

dependency_coverage.horus_support:
Workaround. Horus has no VAT-code list endpoint or VAT-code input. Each invoice line states its VAT treatment through a combination of fields:
- sales and purchases: TaxRate, TaxType ('0: National', '1: European', '2: International') and TaxOrigin;
- purchases only: TaxKind, TaxCondition and TaxConditionValue;
- sales OSS lines only: TaxCountryCode.
Only some combinations are valid. The catalogue is built from the tax-combination files, the two Horus spreadsheets linked from the invoice endpoints (downloaded 13 Oct 2026; appendix C), one list per legislation and direction. The connector owns this catalogue, with ONE id grammar used identically by GET vat-codes (folder-scoped), create_invoice (decode) and get_invoices (encode):
- Sales: 'S-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}', plus '-{TaxCountryCode}' for OSS rows (BE TaxOrigin 13; LU 24, 26, 29; rate and country supplied per transaction). Example: 'S-21-0-0'.
- Purchases: 'P-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}-{TaxKind}-{TaxCondition}-{TaxConditionValue}', with 'x' for a component that is not used. Example: 'P-21-2-0-0-1-true'. On LU COUNTRY rows (TaxCondition 0), the condition value is the country code.
A tax_code is valid only if it is in the folder's list for the invoice direction (otherwise 422); validation follows the files, not the reference TaxOrigin enums.
Other Chift fields: type = sale or purchase (from the prefix); scope from TaxType (0→nat, 1→eu, 2→int); rate = TaxRate; country = TaxCountryCode for OSS rows; reversed could be derived from co-contractor or intra-EU origins (A). deductible_account and payable_account have no Horus source (NA). The catalogue depends on the folder's legislation (BE or LU).
Read rule: build the id from account-histories VatDetail (VatRate, SaleTaxOrigin or PurchaseTaxOrigin, TaxType, TaxCountryCode, TaxCondition, TaxConditionValue) and return it only if exactly one entry of the folder's list matches. VatDetail has no TaxKind, so when several purchase entries match (differing only by TaxKind), or none does, return tax_code = null and keep tax_rate and tax_amount. Never guess, and never return Horus VatDetail.VatCode as the Chift tax_code: VatCode and VatHeading are read-only strings whose meaning is undocumented; no endpoint lists them. Read-side TaxCondition has an extra value '4 = Article'.
Open questions to Horus (H1): confirm the tax-combination files and the LU code discrepancies; the combination for a folder with IsVatLiable=false; is VatCode stable and one-to-one with a combination, and can TaxKind be exposed on read (VatDetail)?

ba_insights: Good structural fit, unusual protocol. Every business object behind the 11 case routes exists in Horus with read and/or write support: third parties, GL accounts, journals, sales and purchase entries, misc operations, analytics on up to 8 dimensions, and open items. But Horus is an RPC API (named methods such as companies.list or invoices.sales.new) where reads with filters are POSTs. Every Chift GET becomes one or more Horus POSTs, so the connector is a translator, not a pass-through.

Authentication is now fully documented, with three points Chift's platform must handle. (1) Each license has its own api_url, returned during OAuth, which must be stored per consumer. (2) The token exchange uses grant_type=auth_code instead of the standard 'authorization_code'. (3) Refresh tokens are single-use and rotate on every refresh, so refreshes must be serialised per consumer; a race can silently disconnect a customer. API rights are those of the authorizing user (an accountant in Horus Office or an entrepreneur in Horus Mobile), so who authorizes decides which folders Chift can see.

Horus documents no pagination. No endpoint has a page, size, cursor or total, history endpoints force month/year windows, and the guides never mention paging. Chift's {items, total, page, size} must be emulated by fetching everything (lists are expected to return their full result, a deduction), filtering, sorting and slicing. Mitigations: gzip, ModifiedAfter incremental sync (only on companies, book entries and account histories) and per-folder caching. Whether Horus silently caps large results is undocumented: a priority-1 question for Horus (H5).

Many Chift routes are composite because the API reference has no invoice read model: no invoice list and no invoice-shaped get. GET /book-entries.info reads one entry by Id in a single call, without the daybook and month window that book-entries.list needs, which simplifies read-back after create and GET attachments. But like a book-entries.list element it returns only the header, totals, due date and references (company, main document, lines). Chift invoices must be rebuilt from book-entries.list (one call per daybook and period), account-histories.list (lines, VAT, analytics, matching), invoices.sales.outstanding.list (payment status, sales only), companies (partner) and documents (PDF). Sideloading (Include, with results under Included) is now documented on 4 endpoints and removes the extra calls for companies, daybooks and folders. Whether line items or IBANs can be sideloaded still has to be confirmed.

Terminology trap that matters in the client conversation. A Horus 'Folder' is Chift's folder (the company whose books are kept). A Horus 'Company' is a client, supplier or beneficiary of that folder: one record with role flags. Because one record holds both roles, Chift's force_merge maps cleanly to updating that record's flags. Daybook = journal, cost schema / cost section = analytic plan / analytic account, account history = entry line, MatchNo = matching number.

VAT codes, payment terms and payment methods are not entities in Horus. VAT is stated on each line as TaxRate + TaxType + TaxOrigin (plus Kind and Condition for purchases, and a country for OSS), with Belgian- and Luxembourg-specific values, and the allowed combinations are published in the two Horus spreadsheets linked from the invoice endpoints (downloaded 13 Oct 2026; appendix C), one list per legislation and direction. The connector must define its own VAT-code catalogue, the biggest functional design decision. The proposal is one synthetic id grammar ('S-21-0-0' for sales, 'P-21-2-0-0-1-true' for purchases) for listing, posting and reading. Horus does not return TaxKind on read, so a purchase code is returned on read only when it is unambiguous; otherwise tax_code is null and the rate and amount are kept. Payment methods become a fixed list from the PaymentMode enum. Payment terms can only be a synthetic list built from the documented delay codes ('30E' etc.), and Horus always needs an explicit due date.

The posting workflow is the main product decision. Horus deliberately creates API entries unconfirmed so the accountant reviews them first, while Chift's create routes default to 'posted' and promise automatic numbering when no invoice number is given. Both are possible in Horus (Confirmed is an optional flag on the invoice and operation creates), so the connector proposes a per-connection posting mode: review (push unconfirmed, proposed default) or direct (confirm 'posted' entries); Chift decides. Horus can auto-number only confirmed operations (misc, bank, financial), not invoices, so a confirmed invoice needs a valid numeric number.

Immutable-ledger behaviour Chift's clients must know about. Updating an invoice or operation creates a new book entry id and deletes the attached document, and Horus itself says to sync on daybook plus entry number rather than on id. Only unconfirmed misc operations created through the API can be deleted, and no deletion feed exists. There is no idempotency key: the connector deduplicates clients on ExternalReference and VAT (Horus refuses duplicate VAT numbers by default) and entries on DocumentNo (a pre-check whenever a number is supplied, and again before any retry). This protection is best-effort: records without a key cannot be found after a timeout and are not retried automatically.

Operationally mature contract, with gaps that are now few and specific. Errors are uniform (200/400/401/403/404/500 with {ErrorType, Details, Message}) and come with explicit retry advice. A written compatibility policy says breaking changes are announced by email and asks for tolerant clients. Still missing: rate limits, result-size caps, the ErrorType catalogue, sideloading paths per endpoint, and any sandbox. Tests run on real data, so Chift needs a test license or test folder from Horus.

Recommended go/no-go framing for the client. With one calibration for all routes (supported = native endpoints with deterministic mapping, no extra live calls per request and nothing emulated; workaround = extra live calls, emulation or a lost capability), only Get folders is Supported; Get analytic plans is a low-complexity workaround (emulated paging over at most 8 rows; Free-type schemas hidden pending C9), and the remaining case routes, including all four create routes, are supported with a workaround. No route is blocked by a missing Horus capability in the documentation reviewed. The real risks are performance on large folders (no paging, unknown caps), VAT-code modelling, the confirmed/numbering policy, foreign-currency amounts on read, and purchase-side outstanding and payment status (ledger-line level only). These should be confirmed with Horus (developer@horus-software.be) and tested on a test license before build (a conditional go with a short gate).
